title: Who pays: power plants and large industrial facilities
parameters: The price is charged on carbon dioxide from fuel burned at (1) fossil-fuel electricity generating units that already report their emissions to EPA by continuous monitoring (40 CFR part 75, the Acid Rain Program's units), and, outside the contiguous states where that program does not reach [EV-CLP-270], generating units that report under part 98 at or above the threshold below, and (2) industrial facilities whose emissions are at least 25,000 tons of CO2-equivalent a year, the threshold of EPA's facility reporting program (40 CFR part 98). It is charged on each covered facility's reported emissions, not on fuel sales, so no upstream fuel tracking is built (working choice, `DEC-2026-11-13-08`; memo 1 B described a charge on fuel sold to power plants). Power plants pay each quarter on their part 75 quarterly reports [EV-CLP-269]. Industrial facilities, which report once a year under part 98 [EV-CLP-268], pay quarterly estimated amounts on the prior year's reported emissions at the quarter's price and settle on the annual report, as estimated taxes are (working choice). R2 itself requires every facility the price covers to keep reporting under parts 75 and 98, as part of the tax base's definition, so the price does not depend on the clean power and climate act or on EPA's rules of the day. Fuel sold to anyone else is not charged
agency: Treasury (IRS) collects; EPA certifies the emissions

title: What is not charged
parameters: Homes, commercial buildings and small businesses are not charged directly, and neither are gasoline and diesel, which Moving America's fuel steps price (MOV-29), or other transport fuel. Facilities under the threshold are not charged. Electricity and covered goods carry the price in their cost; the dividend returns it

title: The price path
status: decided, memo 1: the legacy path kept
parameters: $25 a ton of CO2 in 2030; D7's equal steps to about $46 in 2032; equal steps to $150 in 2037; then 5% a year, nominal. Written in the statute, not delegated

title: Process emissions at covered facilities
status: decided, memo 1 part 1 B: "and their process emissions"; as booked
parameters: Process CO2 and N2O at covered industrial facilities (cement, steel, ammonia, lime, petrochemicals) pay the same price. Their receipts go first to the O5 account that finances the package's net cost, the remainder to the dividend, as booked (CLI-2O.01)

title: The border adjustment
parameters: Imports of the covered goods (steel, aluminum, cement, fertilizer and ammonia, hydrogen, and basic chemicals; working choice: the goods the EU's border charge covers) pay the price on their embodied emissions, less any carbon price paid where they were made. Default emission values by product and country, with lower verified values accepted. Exports of the same goods get a rebate. Built to count as an equivalent price under the EU's border charge
agency: Treasury (CBP collects at entry); EPA sets default values

title: The methane fee
parameters: The Inflation Reduction Act's waste emissions charge (Clean Air Act sec. 136) applies from 2030, undoing the delay to 2034: $1,200 a ton of methane in 2030, $1,350 in 2031, $1,500 from 2032, not indexed, on all methane at oil and gas facilities above 25,000 tons of CO2-equivalent, with no intensity threshold. A facility is exempt for a year if it certifies, on an independent audit and measured reporting, that it meets the leak-prevention standards; a super-emitter event or a failed audit ends the exemption

title: The Climate Dividend: equal per adult, quarterly, tax-free, named
parameters: Every adult 18 and over gets one equal share each quarter, adult dependents included; children are covered by the child benefit (FAM-1), not a share. The payment is called the Climate Dividend in statute and on every deposit and notice. It is not taxable and does not count as income for any federal program (shared rule 1, `DEC-2026-11-12-06`). Size: 80% of the quarter's combustion receipts divided by the adults paid; on the carbon model read about $133 an adult in 2030, $439 in 2035 and $492 in 2040 (nominal, a year; working assumption)
agency: Treasury (IRS and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service)

title: Who is paid, and how, with no application for most people
parameters: Paid on the child benefit's rail and notice (FAM-1.09): to filers from their latest return; automatically to Social Security, SSI, VA and Railroad Retirement beneficiaries from those agencies' payment records; to anyone else on a one-page sign-up at the child benefit's front doors (FAM-1.10). Residents are paid under immigration's table for the plan's universal programs (shared rule 3, `DEC-2026-11-12-07`, memo 6 C), with an individual taxpayer number accepted (working choice). The payment is protected from offset and garnishment as the child benefit is (FAM-1.07; working choice)
agency: Treasury (IRS, Fiscal Service), with SSA, VA and the Railroad Retirement Board

title: Paid first, from a dividend account with a permanent appropriation
parameters: The fee's receipts go to a Climate Dividend account with a permanent, indefinite appropriation and Treasury's standing disbursement authority, so a lapse in appropriations or a later Congress cannot stop a payment without changing the law. **The first payment is a one-time payment, made the way the 2020-21 economic impact payments were** [EV-CLP-056]: to filers from their latest return, and automatically to Social Security, SSI, VA and Railroad Retirement beneficiaries from those agencies' payment records, in the calendar quarter before the price begins, from an advance repaid from the account's receipts within the year. From the child benefit's first monthly payment (no later than July 2030, FAM-1.07) the dividend moves to the shared rail (CLI-2A.02). **The price begins on the first calendar quarter that starts at least six months after enactment and after the first dividend is paid** (working choice): on the working timeline, R2 by about January 2030, so the price begins July 1, 2030 and the first dividend goes out in April-June 2030

title: The 80/20 split
parameters: 80% of the combustion receipts to the dividend; 20% to a transition share, which pays the transition guarantee first (CLI-11.08), then the add-ons (CLI-5F.01) and, from FY2040, the bill credit (CLI-5H.01). Process receipts follow CLI-2O.01

title: The O5 financing bridge, as booked
status: decided, memo 1 part 1 B: process emissions stay priced
parameters: The incremental process and combustion receipts from Package A's measures, less the dividend they carry, finance the package's net cost in their own account (CLI-2O, CXP, as booked). The booking step reruns the accounts for the narrower combustion base

title: The credits, from tax year 2030
status: decided, memo 2 part 1 B; as booked
parameters: *Power and storage:* the technology-neutral production and investment credits (secs. 45Y, 48E) for wind and solar again, and for every clean technology. *Manufacturing:* the advanced manufacturing credit (45X), wind components included, and the 48C allocation. *Homes:* 25C (efficiency and heat pumps) and 25D (rooftop solar and batteries). *Vehicles:* 30D, 25E, 45W and 30C. Each refundable; elective pay (sec. 6417) and transfer (sec. 6418) kept; the household and vehicle credits transferred to the dealer or installer at the point of sale

title: The step-down, published in statute
parameters: Each credit steps down on a schedule tied to the rule that replaces it (working choice, matching the booked path): power credits at full value for projects starting construction through 2034, 60% for 2035-37 and none after, except storage and firm clean power (nuclear, geothermal) at full value through 2039; vehicle credits at full value through 2032, then 75%, 50% and none after 2034 as the fleet standards bind (CLI-4E.01); the household credits at full value through 2034, then for heat pumps in homes under 80% of area median income only, through 2039; 45X and 48C through 2039. No credit is extended by regulation

title: The cost review trigger
parameters: If the credits' outlays and revenue loss run more than 25% above the booked path (`6-cost.md`, part 1) for two fiscal years in a row, Treasury reports to Congress within 90 days and every scheduled step comes forward one year, unless Congress acts within 180 days of the report
agency: Treasury (Office of Tax Analysis), with JCT's estimates

title: Foreign-entity rules against named countries
status: decided, memo 2 part 1 B: the legacy credit set's rule
parameters: The 2025 law's "prohibited foreign entity" tests are replaced by rules written against the countries of concern named in 10 U.S.C. 4872, so that financing is not blocked by broad material-assistance tests

title: Contracts for difference for heavy industry
status: decided, memo 2 part 2 A; as booked
parameters: Competitive rounds for low-carbon steel, cement, aluminum, chemicals and hydrogen. Each contract pays the gap between a strike price and a reference price (the product's market price plus the carbon price paid), and the producer pays back when the reference is above the strike. Terms up to 15 years, timed to furnace and kiln rebuilds; funds obligated at signing; emissions verified independently each year
agency: DOE (Loan Programs Office, now the Office of Energy Dominance Financing)

title: Buy Clean in statute
parameters: Federal construction and federally funded highway projects buy concrete, steel, asphalt and glass under embodied-carbon limits set from environmental product declarations, as GSA's 2023 program did, with limits tightening every three years (working choice)

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: The clean electricity standard: 80% by 2035, 100% by 2040
parameters: Each retail electricity supplier holds clean credits for a share of its sales that rises in a straight line from its 2029 share to 80% in 2035 and to 100% in 2040, then stays there. Clean: wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, nuclear, storage discharging clean power, and fossil generation with capture at its captured share. Credits are the renewable energy certificates the regional tracking systems already issue for state standards, extended to every clean source; no new federal registry (working choice, `DEC-2026-11-13-08`). Suppliers selling under 1 million megawatt-hours a year meet the standard through their wholesale supplier (working choice)

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: DOE (EIA certifies compliance); FERC oversees the tracking systems

title: The capped payment, and where it goes
parameters: A supplier short of credits pays an alternative compliance payment per missing megawatt-hour, capped at $40 in 2025 dollars, indexed to prices (working choice, the carbon model's figure). Treasury collects the payments, and they go to the bill credit (CLI-5H.01) for as long as they are paid: first to bill protection (CLI-5L.01) while it runs, then to the credit itself, so none is stranded when bill protection ends. On the carbon model's run of the decided path, the clean share is 91% in 2040 and 94% in 2045, limited by grid access, not price, so suppliers pay about **$0.11 trillion over 2030-39 and about $29 billion in 2040**, falling slowly after (the carbon model read, `tools/coverage_read.py`; `6-cost.md`, part 2). They are a charge on electricity bills, returned to lower- and moderate-income households

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: Permitting, if the bipartisan package becomes law
parameters: The package's transmission siting and faster review stay. Its permit-certainty section is amended so that an emissions standard, the clean electricity standard, a planned retirement or a rule under this act is never an "interference" with a permit, and any damages it pays are capped per project and per year, with appropriations required above the cap (working choice: the lesser of 10% of the project's sunk cost or $100 million a project a year)

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: DOJ (the Judgment Fund); the permitting agencies

title: Permitting, if it does not
parameters: A narrow permitting title: FERC backstop siting for lines on the national-interest list (CLI-10.03); deadlines for federal decisions on transmission and clean power; a shorter window for court challenges (working choice: 150 days); and no permit-certainty damages

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: The endangerment finding and EPA's authority, in statute
parameters: Congress finds that greenhouse gases endanger public health and welfare, and gives EPA express authority to set standards for vehicles and engines (sec. 202) and power plants (sec. 111), including standards based on generation shifting and averaging. Each rule the act requires has a statutory deadline and a default standard that applies if EPA misses it

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: Vehicle standards' numbers in statute
parameters: Fleet-average greenhouse gas standards for cars and light trucks, and for medium and heavy trucks, written into the statute year by year through 2040, set so that the expected electric share of new sales reaches about 25% of cars in 2032, 50% in 2037 and two-thirds in 2040, and about 5%, 30% and 40% of trucks (working choice: the carbon model's standards). Averaging, banking and trading as in EPA's past rules. No separate sales mandate

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: A clean-heat standard from 2032
parameters: Each manufacturer of heating equipment sold in the United States meets a rising share of heat pumps or other zero-emission heat in its sales, on two schedules (working choices): *space heating* 60% in 2032, rising in equal steps to 100% in 2040; *water heating* from its 2029 national share, rising in equal steps from 2032 to 100% in 2040. Both starting points are checked against AHRI's shipment data before enactment. Credits are tradable among manufacturers within each schedule. *Emergency replacement:* through 2039, a unit the installer certifies as replacing failed equipment of the same kind may be sold outside the share, up to 10% of a manufacturer's sales, so no household is forced into an unplanned conversion when a furnace or water heater fails in winter. Certified through DOE's existing appliance certification database. Low-income replacements are paid by the credits (CLI-1A.01) and Weatherization's heat pumps (CLI-5W.01)

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: The national goals
parameters: Net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, and 61-66% below 2005 by 2035, as the national targets. The act states that no domestic package the project has modeled reaches the 2035 range (the legacy model's best is about 48%), and requires an annual progress report against both

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: EPA reports; the President's budget carries it

title: The national greenhouse gas inventory, a statutory duty
parameters: EPA publishes the national inventory and the state inventories by April 15 each year, and keeps the facility reporting the inventory and the carbon price need (40 CFR part 98, part 75 monitoring). If EPA misses the date, the latest data are published as they stand within 30 days

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: Interregional transfer minimums
status: decided, memo 4 part 1 B: the legacy grid statute
parameters: A statutory minimum transfer capability between neighboring regions, starting from NERC's 2024 study's 35 GW of added capability, with FERC enforcing the schedule and planning it where regions do not file

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

cost_source: 6-cost.md, part 1 (no direct cost; FERC is fee-funded)

title: Utility rules
parameters: A performance-based ratemaking standard that state commissions must consider (PURPA sec. 111(d)), with shared savings for grid-enhancing technologies; no ratepayer-funded lobbying or advertising; minimum governance and transparency rules for regional transmission organizations, with intervenor funding; mandatory cyber standards for distribution utilities and large inverters, with funding for small co-ops

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

cost_source: 6-cost.md, part 1 (no direct cost; FERC is fee-funded)

title: Large new loads pay their own grid costs
parameters: A new load of 20 MW or more, or new service of that size at an existing large load, pays for the generation capacity and the wires its connection requires, under tariffs the state commission or FERC approves, in every market. In ERCOT, where FERC has no rate jurisdiction, the act directs the Public Utility Commission of Texas to apply the same rule to every ERCOT utility's large-load tariffs, as a condition of the federal grid money and credits that reach ERCOT projects (working choice; the legacy grid statute's clarification that the large-load floor reaches ERCOT utilities). Other customers' rates may not carry those costs

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: FERC; state commissions; the Public Utility Commission of Texas for ERCOT
cost_source: 6-cost.md, part 1 (no direct cost; FERC is fee-funded)

title: The first grid tranche
status: decided, memo 4 part 1 B; as booked
parameters: $25 billion of grants, $100 billion of direct loans and $20 billion of capacity contracts for transmission, interconnection and grid upgrades, 2030-39; booked at about $39 billion in deficit terms
agency: DOE (Grid Deployment Office for grants and capacity contracts; the Loan Programs Office for loans)

title: The second tranche, authorized up front, released on milestones
parameters: $40 billion of grants, $200 billion of loans and $40 billion of capacity contracts, released only when the first tranche's lines are under construction on schedule and the transfer minimums are on track (working choice: DOE certifies each milestone and publishes the evidence)

title: The public builders' borrowing
parameters: TVA's bond limit raised from $30 billion, set in 1979, to $60 billion (working choice); Bonneville's Treasury borrowing raised by $10 billion and WAPA's transmission borrowing from $3.25 billion to $10 billion, both for transmission (working choices). Costs are recovered from the users of the lines, as today

title: Public power as builder of last resort
parameters: DOE keeps a national-interest list of lines, drawn from its needs study and FERC-approved plans. If no regional builder files to build a listed line within two years, the federal builder builds it and recovers its cost through transmission rates: rates FERC approves, or, for a line inside ERCOT, where FERC has no rate jurisdiction, ERCOT's transmission cost-of-service charge that the Public Utility Commission of Texas approves for every transmission owner there. The builder is WAPA's Transmission Infrastructure Program, extended nationwide, with TVA and Bonneville building in their own regions: no new federal corporation (working choice, `DEC-2026-11-13-08`). WAPA's program can build, finance or partner on lines today but has mostly lent and partnered; the act funds and staffs it to build (`5-delivery.md`, part 2). It uses the existing federal siting backstops, not new eminent domain

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: DOE (WAPA); TVA; Bonneville; FERC, or the Public Utility Commission of Texas for ERCOT

title: An automatic energy bill credit
parameters: A household enrolled in SNAP, SSI, LIHEAP or the Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations (whose households cannot take SNAP in the same month [EV-CLP-267]) at any time in the prior year gets a yearly credit on its energy bill, with no separate application. Sized from the state's (or tribe's) own LIHEAP benefit table toward 6% of income, using the household's income already on file. **A fixed yearly sum** (working choice): if the matched households' credits exceed the allotment, every credit is scaled down in the same proportion, so the cost is known and the formula is published (`6-cost.md`, memo 5 B, for the matched count and the average credit). Paid by the state LIHEAP office, or by the tribe for tribes that run their own LIHEAP grant [EV-CLP-055], to the household's utility or fuel vendor under the vendor agreements they already hold, or to the household where heat is included in rent. Others apply as now. Money: LIHEAP's block grant made mandatory at about $12 billion a year from FY2031 (R3, with the first credits in winter 2030-31), indexed (working assumption), against about $4 billion today, plus the standard's payments (CLI-3A.02)
agency: HHS (LIHEAP), through the states and tribal grantees; SNAP records from the states, SSI records from SSA, FDPIR records from the tribal agencies

title: Cooling counts, and water help is permanent
status: decided, memo 5 B: the legacy add-ons
parameters: Summer cooling counts equally with heating in the credit; the low-income household water assistance program becomes permanent, paid the same way to water utilities

title: Low-income heat pumps through Weatherization
parameters: DOE's Weatherization Assistance Program may fund heat pumps, about 250,000 low-income homes a year from 2031 (the carbon model's working figure), on the booked $84 billion

title: Bill protection, and when it ends
parameters: Low- and moderate-income households get added help while the standard and the price raise bills, funded first by the standard's capped payments (CLI-3A.02) and paid as part of the same bill credit (CLI-5H.01), not as a second program. It ends when EIA's average residential price, adjusted for inflation, is below its 2029 level for two years in a row, not on a fixed date; the standard's payments then continue to the bill credit (CLI-3A.02)

title: The rest of the add-ons, as booked
status: decided, memo 5 B: the legacy add-ons
parameters: The transmission investment credit for lines in FERC-approved plans, the 45X expansions, the household resilience credit, agricultural research and technical assistance, critical-minerals offtake and adaptation finance, as booked; the minerals and adaptation-finance lines borrowed for as time-limited capital (CLI-5F, C37)

title: Disaster capital: the mitigation fund, wildfire work and buyouts
parameters: A standing mitigation fund of $3-6 billion a year, paid partly by formula with a floor for every state and tribe so small places do not lose to grant-writing capacity, partly to large competitive projects; wildfire risk reduction of $1.5-3.5 billion a year above today; voluntary buyouts and relocation of $1.9-4.7 billion a year, 2030-39. Mandatory money that cannot be withheld

title: The permanent disaster pieces
parameters: The post-disaster mitigation share from 15% to 20%; premium help for low- and moderate-income primary residences under the flood program, sized to income, not a cap on the rate; extreme heat as an eligible hazard; one survivor application and estimate-based public assistance; and premium help for wind, wildfire and hail for low- and moderate-income owners and renters in high-risk counties. The premium help rides R2 with the disaster capital; the other rules ride the clean power and climate act

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: FEMA (NFIP for flood premium help); Treasury for wind, wildfire and hail help (CLI-7C.01's office)

title: NFIP's debt resolved, with a long reauthorization
parameters: The program's debt to Treasury (about $22.5 billion) cancelled together with a reauthorization to 2035 and a reserve rule; scored at about $2.2 billion

title: A capped federal reinsurance facility
parameters: Treasury reinsures insurers' residential wind, wildfire and hail losses (earthquake where a state opts in) in the layer between a state-level 1-in-100-year and 1-in-250-year industry loss; insurers keep 10% of the layer; an annual cap of $150 billion; premiums priced to expected loss; recoupment after a draw, as under the terrorism program. Offered only in states that meet CLI-8.01's codes test, which R2 writes into the facility's own terms (if the Byrd rule strikes it, the facility waits for the act). Its $75-150 billion contingent liability is disclosed in every fiscal test, not scored
agency: Treasury (the Federal Insurance Office, which runs the terrorism program)

title: Codes as a condition, and a flood standard for federal rebuilding
parameters: A state keeps the wind, wildfire and hail premium help and access to the reinsurance facility if it adopts current hazard-resistant building codes within three years of enactment; new federal rebuilding aid meets a forward-looking federal flood risk standard, written into statute. Conditions attach to new aid only

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: Who is covered, from records already filed
status: decided, memo 7 B, contractors included by Espen
parameters: A worker who loses their job when a covered facility closes or permanently cuts its workforce, on or after January 1, 2030: coal mines; coal- and gas-fired power plants; petroleum refineries; coal and gas processing plants. Covered: the facility's employees, and workers employed by a contractor who worked at the facility for at least six of the last twelve months (working choice). A permanent cut is a WARN Act plant closing or mass layoff at the site; for a facility too small for the WARN Act, the same events by the same definitions, reported to the state. Eligibility comes from the closure notice the employer files and the payroll records for the site: the facility's owner lists its site contractors in the notice, and each contractor files its site payroll with the state within 30 days, under the same remedy as the owner (`5-delivery.md`, part 4). A contractor's worker left off a file may show coverage from their own pay stubs. No application beyond confirming the record; no means test

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

agency: Labor (ETA), with the state unemployment agencies

title: The income guarantee: 90% for two years
status: decided, memo 7 B, with Espen's parameters
parameters: For two years from the job loss: *in a new job,* a top-up equal to 90% of the old hourly wage less the new hourly wage, paid for the hours actually worked, up to the old weekly schedule; *in approved training,* 90% of the old weekly pay; *otherwise,* unemployment benefits only. Unemployment benefits count toward the 90%, so no one gets more than 90% of their old pay. The old wage is capped at twice the national median wage (BLS's annual figure, about $114,000 a year in 2030 on the working assumption). No suitable-job test: any job counts. Paid monthly on the worker's statement of hours and wage with a pay stub, checked after the fact against the state's quarterly wage records
agency: Labor (ETA); state unemployment agencies pay, as Labor's agents

title: Retraining money
parameters: Up to $20,000 for training from a provider on the state's existing eligible training provider list, paid through an individual training account at an American Job Center

title: A pension bridge at 55
parameters: A covered worker 55 or older at the job loss with a defined-benefit pension may draw it unreduced from the job loss; Treasury reimburses the plan the cost of waiving the early-retirement reduction, through the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation as its agent (working choice). A worker 55 or older without one may take CLI-11.02's training-level support for the full two years without enrolling in training

title: Published counts with a review trigger, not a job test
parameters: Labor publishes each year, by state and facility type: workers covered, the path each took (job, training, bridge, none), the average top-up, and the hours and wages of the new jobs. If, in any year, more than half of top-up dollars go to jobs under 20 hours a week or paying under the federal poverty line for a full-time worker (working choice), Labor reports to Congress with options within 90 days. Nothing changes automatically

title: Replacement of the lost local tax base
parameters: A county, school district or other local taxing unit losing property tax from a closed covered facility gets a yearly payment equal to the lost tax in the first year after closure, falling by 10 points a year to zero after ten years, measured from the assessor's last roll before closure. Paid through Interior's payments-in-lieu-of-taxes office, which already pays counties each year (working choice, `DEC-2026-11-13-08`)

title: Refinancing retiring coal plants
parameters: The Federal Financing Bank buys ratepayer-backed bonds that a state commission approves to refinance a retiring coal plant's remaining book value, at Treasury's rate plus a small spread, if the plant retires on a fixed date and is not mothballed, and at least a tenth of the proceeds goes to the plant's workers and community (working choice, after New Mexico's San Juan bonds)

title: Paid first from the transition share
parameters: The guarantee's payments are drawn from the carbon price's 20% transition share before any other use; the general fund pays any shortfall. The guarantee is an entitlement: it does not depend on the share's size

vehicle.note: the clean power and climate act (regular order)

title: Conservation payments for methane and soil carbon
parameters: Mandatory USDA conservation funding for practices that cut methane and nitrous oxide and build soil carbon, through the existing conservation programs; about $31 billion over FY2030-39

title: Reforestation
parameters: Reforestation and forest restoration on federal and partner land, 2030-39; about $25 billion
